# Jubilees Chapter 33 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Reuben's transgression; sexual purity laws; deaths of Rachel and Leah

---

**33:1** Jacob went to the southern land and dwelt at Migdal-Eder, between Ephrath and Bethlehem.

**33:2** Rachel died there and was buried in the land of Ephrath, which is Bethlehem. Jacob erected a standing stone over her grave, on the road above it — it is the standing stone of Rachel's grave to this day.

**33:3** In those days Reuben lay with Bilhah the concubine of his father. Jacob heard what had happened and was angry, and he was deeply grieved.

**33:4** Jacob rebuked Reuben, and Reuben repented and confessed his sin, and Jacob forgave him. But Jacob did not go in to Bilhah again after this.

**33:5** For he counted the defilement as exceedingly great, because Reuben had lain in the bed of his father's concubine; and he separated himself from her.

**33:6** Because of this, the children of Israel are commanded not to defile themselves with their father's wife — not to uncover their father's nakedness.

**33:7** For it is unclean: any man who lies with his father's wife has uncovered his father's nakedness, and such a man shall be put to death.

**33:8** Concerning a man who lies with his daughter-in-law: it is written and ordained that both of them shall be burned with fire.

**33:9** Concerning all forms of sexual immorality and impurity and every unlawful union — these are written and ordained in the heavenly tablets.

**33:10** After Rachel's death, Jacob took Leah and went with her to his father Isaac. Isaac was exceedingly glad to see Jacob and Leah and all of Jacob's sons.

**33:11** Jacob came to his father Isaac at Mamre — which is Hebron — in the fourth year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee.

**33:12** Isaac was very old and exceedingly advanced in years; his eyes were completely dim and he could not see.

**33:13** Jacob said to his father Isaac: "Do not be sorrowful, my father, for I have returned to you. I have much livestock — cattle and sheep and flocks — and your grandsons have grown up."

**33:14** Isaac prayed over Jacob and blessed him with joy, and Jacob rejoiced before his father all the days of his life.

**33:15** In the first year of the fourth week of the forty-fifth jubilee, Leah died. Jacob buried her in the cave of Machpelah at Mamre — with Abraham and Sarah, and with Isaac and Rebekah his mother — by night.

**33:16** They mourned Leah deeply, and Jacob mourned her greatly, and her sons also wept for her.

**33:17** The LORD comforted Jacob after the death of Leah.

---

*LOGOS notes: The Reuben incident follows Genesis 35:22 closely but Jubilees emphasizes Jacob's forgiveness and separation from Bilhah, moderating Genesis 49:4. The legal section (vv.6-9) is the Jubilees author's characteristic move: every narrative infraction becomes the foundation for a law. Leah's death and burial at Machpelah (vv.15-16) is unique to Jubilees.*
